units.translation: For it is pitiful that the ancient city should be hurled to Hades, a spear's prey, a slave, destroyed dishonorably by an Achaean man, by divine will, into dry ash.
But you may praise or blame me alike.

where in M ψεδυρα/ψεθυρα [whispering] without accent. Stanley rightly reads ψεδυραί [whispering], since μοῖρ᾽ Αφροδίτας [the portion of Aphrodite] can more easily do without an epithet than τρίβοι ἐρώτων [the paths of love], although the scholiast reads ψεδυρά [whispering], 'Harmonia partakes of Aphrodite; and she is false because lovers tell many lies,' and similarly in Hesychius ψέδυρα [whispering] (changed to ψέδυρος [whispering] by Musurus): ψίθυρος [whispering]. The superscript in Me alludes to ψίθυρα [whispering], which means whispering and slanderous words: see Thes. vol. 8 p. 1903. Ἀφροδίτην ψίθυρον [whispering Aphrodite] and Ἔρωτα ψίθυρον [whispering Eros] were worshipped at Athens, as the grammarians cited in Thes. record, ibid. p. 1905.
And to Harmonia is given the portion of Aphrodite, the whispering paths of love.
ἡ Αρμονία μετέχει τῆς Ἀφροδίτης · ψευδὴς δὲ, ὅτι πολλὰ ψεύδονται οἱ ἐρῶντες [Harmonia partakes of Aphrodite; and she is false because lovers tell many lies]
stammering, lisping. Improperly ψελλόν [stammering] is said of what we do not understand, no more, that is, than the words of a stammerer, as Stephanus explains in Thes. vol. 8 p. 1856.

Thus where the scholiast explains it by ἄσημον, ἄναρθρον [unclear, inarticulate], and the Antiatticist noted in Bekker's Anecdota p. 116, 18: ψελλός [stammering]: Aeschylus in Prometheus. He has used the word of what is not clearly spoken.
And if any of these things is stammering and hard to find, repeat it and learn it clearly.
ψελλός [stammering]: Aeschylus in Prometheus. He has used the word of what is not clearly spoken.
For the mouth of Zeus does not know how to speak falsely.
Of things invented falsely or fabricated for any purpose.
Do not pity me and warm me with false words.
There is no way I could call false things noble.
There is a time when god honors falsehood.
And many false feasts of the raging jaw they snatched from the mouth in first joy.
Am I a false prophet, a door-knocking babbler?
How you deceived the Persians in your mind.
Being a prophet, I will not lie.
And many, I think, were deceived, the woman who cleansed the swaddling clothes of the child.
You will come to a violent river, not falsely named.
Or indeed Justice would be justly called falsely named.
The gods call you Prometheus under a false name.
Burned from Ilium, he sends to his friends a small, tearful scraping.
